---
title: "Energy use of a note"
description: "See roughly how much electricity and carbon the AI model used for a note, and what the estimate covers."
---

OmicsBase estimates how much electricity the AI model used to write the answers in a note, and the carbon emissions that go with it.

## Where to see it {#where}

### For one note {#one-note}

Open the usage card of the note. It is the card that shows the note's tokens and your balance. It has a line like this:

> This note: about 2–6 Wh, 1–3 g CO₂e (estimate)

<!-- screenshot: note-usage-energy — the usage card of a note with the line "This note: about 2–6 Wh, 1–3 g CO₂e (estimate)"; highlight the line -->

Electricity is in watt-hours (Wh); one Wh runs a 10-watt LED lamp for six minutes. Carbon is in grams of carbon dioxide equivalent (g CO₂e). Each figure is a range, such as 2–6, and the real value is likely to lie within it; see [Why a range](#ranges).

The line counts everything the model did for the note: the answers, the look-ups and other steps in between, the summaries and the note's title.

### For your account {#account}

1. Click your name in the sidebar.
   A menu opens.
2. Click **Settings**, then **Account**.
3. Look under **Billing**, below **Token balance**.
   You see the total for all your notes.

<!-- screenshot: settings-energy-total — Settings, Account tab, Billing section with the energy total under Token balance; highlight the total -->

### When it says "partial" {#partial}

Some models, such as free models and very new ones, have no estimate. If a note used such a model, the line says **partial** and the numbers cover only the part of the note that could be estimated, so the real total is higher.

## What the numbers are {#method}

The numbers are estimates made with the method of [EcoLogits](https://ecologits.ai/latest/), an open-source project that estimates the environmental footprint of AI models.

For each answer, the method uses the model that wrote it, how much text it wrote and how long that took.

### What is counted {#counted}

- The electricity of the servers while the model writes your answer.
- The electricity of the data centre around them, such as cooling.
- A share of the making of the hardware.

### What is not counted {#not-counted}

- Training the model.
- Sending data over the network.
- Your computer or phone.
- Running the R cells of the note, which also uses electricity.

### Why a range {#ranges}

The companies behind models such as Claude, Gemini and GPT do not publish the size of their models. The method estimates their size and gives a low and a high value.

For open models the size is known, so the range is narrower.

### Why the carbon figure is rough {#carbon}

How much carbon one Wh causes depends on where the electricity is made. OmicsBase does not know which data centre answered your request, so the method uses an average for the provider or, where there is none, for the world.

For a single request, the carbon figure can be several times too high or too low. Totals over many notes are steadier than the figure for one note.

### Other effects {#other-impacts}

The EcoLogits method also estimates water use, primary energy and the use of minerals and metals. OmicsBase shows only electricity and carbon in the note.

## How to use the numbers {#use}

- Use the numbers to compare notes, for example to see that one note used about ten times more than another. They are too uncertain to report as measured values.
- A smaller model usually uses less. See [Choose a model](models.qmd).
